newsitem.title: USA: Fire blazes in scenic California forest.
newsitem.headline: Fire blazes in scenic California forest.

text.p: About 1,000 firefighters, backed by helicopters and air tankers, battled a fierce wildfire in California's scenic Los Padres National Forest on Thursday, officials said.
Fire officials reported good progress in fighting the 1,700 acre (690 hectares) blaze but said it was only 10 percent contained and could not estimate when it would be fully under control.
A Class One fire team -- a national interagency team experienced in fighting large fires -- was scheduled to take over fighting the fire on Friday morning.
The fire is burning in Los Padres National Forest just south of Big Sur, a picturesque area on the California coast popular with hikers and campers.
Officials suspect arson as the cause of the fire which broke out near Highway 1 on Monday night and spread quickly in rugged, inaccessible terrain about 150 miles (240 kms) south of San Francisco.

One home, four outbuildings and one vehicle were confirmed lost, said Maeton Freel, a spokesman for Los Padres National Forest. He said there were another 15 to 17 homes scattered within the fire area, but firefighters had not been able to see whether they had been destroyed.
One firefighter suffered a sprained ankle, Freel said.

Firefighters were using 11 air tankers and six helicopters to bombard the blaze with water and fire retardant. The fire has been moving inland, away from populated areas, but has encroached on backwoods areas of the Fort Hunter Liggett army base, officials said.

Freel said the northern flank of the fire was "holding pretty well" but the fire was running along a ridge toward the south. Firefighters planned to set backfires to try to halt the fire's progress, he said.
